newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Republicans file lawsuit to stop labor ads.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Republicans file lawsuit to stop labor ads.

text.p: House Republicans filed suit in federal court Thursday seeking to force the Federal Election Commission to act on its charges that labor unions had illegally spent millions of dollars to aid Democrats.

The National Republican Congressional Committee said the FEC failed to act on five complaints the committee filed against a multimillion-dollar AFL-CIO advertising campaign it charged was designed to help Democrats win control of Congress.

The AFL-CIO has committed $35 million to what it calls voter education efforts, including television and radio advertisements and grassroots organizing. Much of the hard- hitting television advertising has been targeted to the districts of vulnerable House Republicans.

"The AFL-CIO Washington bosses have set a price tag on Congress -- $35 million from compulsory union dues forced from the federation's 13 million members," said NRCC chairman Bill Paxon, a New York Republican representative.
"This is the most overt power grab in the history of American politics," he said in a statement. The NRCC provides funding and expertise for Republican House candidates.

The AFL-CIO dismissed the suit as a publicity stunt on the part of the NRCC, saying its advertising was designed to highlight issues, not political candidates, and was free speech protected by the constitution.

"The NRCC's complaints against the AFL-CIO have no legal basis and were designed to only score political points for Republican candidates who are unwilling to address the important policy issues," said AFL-CIO general counsel Jonathan Hiatt in a statement.

Labor officials have said their efforts were designed to educate voters and union members of the issues at stake in the November elections. Unions historically have been a main source of campaign contributions for Democrats.
Paxon said the NRCC filed its first complaint against the AFL-CIO seven months ago.
The NRCC said the AFL-CIO was spending compulsory union dues to influence an election and coordinated with the Democratic party and individual candidates, in violation of election statutes.
